transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Cobalt Head of ML), Tom Reyes (Cobalt VP Eng), Lena Ortiz (Cobalt Security Architect)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): quick discovery call; customer evaluating models and deployment modes; asks about 64k/128k context, multilingual, tool-calling, and security.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. i'm maya from redwood, and ravi is our solutions engineer — quick intros and then we can jump into the model questions.
[00:14] Aisha: hi, i'm aisha, heads up — we've been evaluating a few open models, need something that handles 30k-plus context, multilingual, and can call out to internal tools (inventory, db lookups). low tolerance for hallucination on product-critical prompts.
[00:30] Tom: and hi from eng — timeline is Q2 POC then decision in Q3. cost is important but reliability and security are blockers.
[00:42] Ravi: great, quick framing: we support hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (vpc/on-prem) deployments. model selection ties into deployment — e.g., very long contexts and data residency often push folks toward Dedicated or Private.
[00:58] Lena: security question up front — we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs. Any red flags?
[01:10] Maya: we are SOC2, support SAML/Okta, KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private; hosted has encryption at rest and in-transit and customer-managed keys in enterprise tiers. i'll put links in the follow-up.
[01:25] Aisha: thanks. on models — we've been running internal tests with Llama3-70b, Mistral-large, and Falcon-40b. curious about Redwood's verified models and quantization profiles.
[01:39] Ravi: good set. a few notes: Llama3 variants scale well for instruction tasks; Mistral has good throughput/cost tradeoffs; Falcon is strong but sometimes needs heavier post-processing. we provide performance profiles per model (cpu/gpu, latency/tokens, cost estimate) and recommended quantization for Dedicated/private.
[01:58] Tom: what about context length? we need approx 64k for full conversation history and want the option to test 128k in a POC.
[02:12] Ravi: we can run models with 64k easily on Dedicated/private with the right kernel selection and memory configs; for 128k it's more model- and hardware-dependent. we often use chunked KV caching and prefix caching to avoid re-encoding the whole context.
[02:29] Aisha: are there open models that practically support 128k today? we've seen some experimental Llama forks and Mixtral announcements.
[02:42] Ravi: there are a handful — some Llama3-derived checkpoints and Mixtral have experimental long-context variants. also a lot depends on whether you accept a hybrid approach: keep the long history in an external vector DB and only materialize relevant chunks into the active context. that reduces compute and keeps latency predictable.
[03:02] Aisha: hmm, we prefer true long context for thread continuity. latency target is sub-1s for short replies, but for long-context summarization we can tolerate 2-3s on a dedicated infra.
[03:18] Ravi: that matches other customers. hosted can hit low latency but shared capacity may fluctuate; Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and you can pin specific model versions and kernel configs. Private (on-prem) gives max data control but adds ops overhead.
[03:36] Tom: any streaming/function-calling limitations across models? we need tool-calling to our internal orchestration and structured output for actions.
[03:48] Ravi: function/tool calling is supported at the Redwood API layer — we have structured output and tooling for safe function invocation; models vary in how reliably they follow function schemas. our SE team runs test suites for function-calling quality per model and we can share the results.
[04:05] Lena: and from security standpoint, function-calling has to be constrained by RBAC and allowed endpoints. how does redwood handle that?
[04:16] Maya: in Dedicated/Private you can configure network egress and RBAC so model agents only call approved endpoints. we also have request-level auditing in Redwood Console.
[04:27] Aisha: ok good. cost — can you ballpark cost differences between models for 1M tokens per month?
[04:36] Ravi: rough rule: throughput-optimized models (Mistral variants) can be 30-50% cheaper per-token versus generalist Llama3 in certain quantized configs. Falcon sometimes needs more expensive infra. we'll give a model-by-model estimate in the pricing sheet.
[04:54] Tom: curious about quantization and quality tradeoffs. we've seen 4-bit quant hurt generation fidelity occasionally.
[05:06] Ravi: agreed — we recommend mixed approaches: 4-bit for non-critical inference, 8-bit or bfloat16 for instruction-heavy or hallucination-sensitive flows. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles per workload and monitor quality regressions.
[05:24] Aisha: multilingual: we need reliable Spanish, Portuguese, French, and occasional Mandarin support. tokenization mismatch is a real pain when you fine-tune or prompt-engineer.
[05:37] Ravi: many of the open models have coverage; Llama3 and some Mistral forks do well multilingual. but there are per-language differences; we recommend running representative prompts — we'll run that as part of the benchmark.
[05:50] Aisha: perfect. also, can Redwood host private function endpoints for tool-calling or do we need to expose our services?
[05:59] Maya: for Dedicated and Private you can keep services private in your VPC and we can configure NAT/proxies for outbound calls. Hosted requires exposing a stable endpoint or using a secure connector; we have documented patterns for that.
[06:15] Tom: what's the typical SE benchmark you run — latency, tokens/sec, cost, and failure mode?
[06:23] Ravi: we run per-model tests: cold vs warm latency, throughput at different batch sizes, memory usage for different context lengths, function-calling accuracy metrics, and a hallucination/regression eval on your prompt set. we'll include logs and kernel-level traces for Dedicated.
[06:38] Aisha: sounds good. for the POC we want: (1) 64k end-to-end conversational test, (2) multilingual accuracy on 4 languages, (3) function-calling reliability test.
[06:50] Maya: noted. i'll make that the POC success criteria in the follow-up.
[06:57] Tom: any redwood-managed options for model updates? we don't want surprise regressions mid-quarter.
[07:06] Ravi: we support pinned model versions and can do canary rollouts. Redwood Console has regression alerts tied to eval sets so you can block upgrades until you sign off.
[07:20] Aisha: excellent. any case studies with similar profiles (multilingual + long context)?
[07:27] Maya: we have a retailer and a healthcare customer who've done 64k experiments; i'll share redacted case notes. one example used Dedicated for latency guarantees and kept PHI on Private infra.
[07:40] Lena: quick legal note — we may need a Data Processing Agreement and specifics about logs retention for audit.
[07:48] Maya: absolutely, we'll include the DPA template and retention options.
[07:54] Ravi: a couple of technical caveats — some long-context runs hit GPU memory limits and require model sharding or sequence-slicing; those add complexity but we have patterns. also quantized kernels sometimes change memory footprints, so we test configurations.
[08:10] Tom: do you support multi-model routing? e.g., cheap model for retrieval + high-quality model for final answer?
[08:18] Ravi: yes, smart routing is built-in — route by latency/cost/quality and do automatic fallback. it's common to use a cheaper base model for retrieval or candidate generation and a stronger model for finalization.
[08:32] Aisha: that's promising. any known gotchas for multilingual + tool-calling? sometimes models hallucinate the function call or produce malformed JSON.
[08:43] Ravi: yep — we do schema enforcement at the API layer and have runtime validators; still, model selection influences reliability, and we capture post-call validation metrics in Console.
[08:56] Maya: i'm going to recap the next steps and actions — we'll send pricing and security docs, ravi will run a 64k and 10k token benchmark across Llama3, Mistral-large and Falcon-40b on your sample dataset, and we schedule a POC scoping call with your infra + security.
[09:12] Tom: sounds good; let's aim for early april for results.
[09:18] Aisha: one more small ask — can you include sample prompts for function-calling best practices?
[09:24] Ravi: yes, we'll include examples and a small test harness so you can run local validations.
[09:30] Lena: will you also include network diagrams for Dedicated vs Private? that helps our architecture review.
[09:36] Maya: yes, we'll add that.

[Later timestamps, rough summaries capturing the middle of the call and some cross talk and imperfect transcription]
[30:02] Ravi: (on benchmark plan) we'll do cold/warm, 1-shot/limited context runs, and measure p95/p50 latencies; expect to see Mistral cheaper on throughput, Llama3 stronger on instruction-following, Falcon ok but sometimes needs engineering for hallucination.
[40:15] Aisha: (inaudible) — just to confirm, will dedicated let us bring our own keys for encryption?
[40:25] Maya: yes for Dedicated and Private you can provide keys via KMS/HSM; hosted enterprise tier supports bring-your-own-keys as well.
[48:50] Tom: (notes) make sure we include cost per 1k tokens across configs and breakdown of infra types (A100 vs H100 vs L4).
[55:10] Ravi: we'll include recommended hardware mapping per model and context length — e.g., H100 for 128k experiments, A100 or L4 for 64k depending on batch.
[60:00] Maya: thanks everyone — recap: we'll send pricing, security pack, case studies, and a benchmark plan; customer will share sample data and confirm POC stakeholders. i'll follow up with a calendar invite for the scoping.
[60:20] Aisha: appreciate it, talk soon.
[60:28] Tom: thanks, bye.
